114| def _first_doc(path: Path) -> str:
115|     try:
116|         text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[:1200]
117|     except OSError:
118|         return ""
119|     if '"""' not in text:
120|         return ""
121|     a = text.find('"""')
122|     b = text.find('"""', a + 3)
123|     if b < 0:
124|         return ""
125|     block = text[a + 3:b].strip().splitlines()
126|     return " ".join(x.strip() for x in block[:3])[:240]
127| 
128| 
129| def _subtools(path: Path) -> list[str]:
130|     """Argparse choices + public def names (the loved subtools)."""
131|     try:
132|         raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
133|     except OSError:
134|         return []
135|     found: list[str] = []
136|     for m in re.finditer(r'choices\s*=\s*\[([^\]]+)\]', raw):
137|         for tok in re.findall(r'["\']([a-zA-Z][\w-]{1,40})["\']', m.group(1)):
138|             if tok not in found:
139|                 found.append(tok)
140|     try:
141|         tree = ast.parse(raw)
142|     except SyntaxError:
143|         return found[:24]
144|     for node in tree.body:
145|         if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and not node.name.startswith("_"):
146|             if node.name not in found:
147|                 found.append(node.name)
148|     return found[:24]
149|

151| def _imports(path: Path) -> list[str]:
152|     try:
153|         raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
154|     except OSError:
155|         return []
156|     mods = re.findall(r"(?:from|import)\s+mag\.([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)", raw)
157|     out: list[str] = []
158|     for m in mods:
159|         if m not in out:
160|             out.append(m)
161|     return out[:16]

164| def scan_clis() -> list[dict[str, str]]:
165|     rows: list[dict[str, str]] = []
166|     for p in sorted(MAG.glob("*.py")):
167|         if p.name.startswith("_"):
168|             continue
169|         try:
170|             raw = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
171|         except OSError:
172|             continue
173|         if 'if __name__ == "__main__"' not in raw:
174|             continue
175|         rows.append({
176|             "id": p.stem,
177|             "cmd": f"python -m mag.{p.stem}",
178|             "origin": _first_doc(p),
179|             "family": "scanned",
180|         })
181|     return rows

184| def compile_fabric() -> dict[str, Any]:
185|     """Crown jewels + subtools + import ribs. The copy of tools we love — Mag's own topology."""
186|     from tools import TOOL_MAP
187| 
188|     nodes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
189|     edges: list[dict[str, str]] = []
190|     for c in CROWN:
191|         fn = CROWN_MODULES.get(c["id"])
192|         path = MAG / fn if fn else None
193|         subs = _subtools(path) if path and path.is_file() else []
194|         imps = _imports(path) if path and path.is_file() else []
195|         nodes.append({**c, "module": fn or "", "subtools": subs, "imports_mag": imps})
196|         for other in imps:
197|             edges.append({"from": c["id"], "to": other, "kind": "import-rib"})
198|     nodes.append({
199|         "id": "agent-tools",
200|         "family": "agent",
201|         "cmd": "tools.TOOL_MAP via mag.agent_cli",
202|         "origin": "Coding-seat toolbelt: fs + shell + swarm sense.",
203|         "subtools": sorted(TOOL_MAP.keys()),
204|         "imports_mag": [],
205|     })
206|     mermaid = ["graph LR"]
207|     for e in edges[:80]:
208|         mermaid.append(f"  {e['from']}-->{e['to']}")
209|     fabric = {
210|         "ok": True,
211|         "schema": FABRIC_SCHEMA,
212|         "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00", "Z"),
213|         "law": "Fabric is Mag's own topology copy. Adapt contracts; do not clone foreign thrones.",
214|         "nodes": nodes,
215|         "edges": edges,
216|         "mermaid": "\n".join(mermaid),
217|         "n_nodes": len(nodes),
218|         "n_edges": len(edges),
219|     }
220|     FABRIC.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
221|     FABRIC.write_text(json.dumps(fabric, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
222|     fabric["path"] = _rel_posix(FABRIC)
223|     return fabric
224| 
225| 
226| def compile_catalog() -> dict[str, Any]:
227|     scanned = scan_clis()
228|     seen = {c["id"] for c in CROWN}
229|     extra = [r for r in scanned if r["id"] not in seen]
230|     fabric = compile_fabric()
231|     out = {
232|         "ok": True,
233|         "schema": SCHEMA,
234|         "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00", "Z"),
235|         "law": "OpenClaw LOADs this catalog. Host Mag venv RUNS cmds. /mag is read-only.",
236|         "host": r".\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m mag.<id>",
237|         "crown": CROWN,
238|         "fabric_path": fabric.get("path"),
239|         "fabric_n_nodes": fabric.get("n_nodes"),
240|         "fabric_n_edges": fabric.get("n_edges"),
241|         "scanned_cli_n": len(scanned),
242|         "scanned_extra_n": len(extra),
243|         "scanned_extra": extra,
244|         "dashboard": {
245|             "body": "http://127.0.0.1:8765/",
246|             "fleet_mermaid": "http://127.0.0.1:8765/  GET /api/v1/fleet/hypervisor",
247|             "game": "dashboard h_game / h_table_view",
248|         },
249|     }
250|     OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
251|     OUT.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
252|     out["path"] = _rel_posix(OUT)
253|     return out
254| 
255| 
256| def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
257|     import sys
258|     args = list(argv if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:])
259|     cmd = args[0] if args else "compile"
260|     if cmd != "compile":
261|         print("usage: python -m mag.openclaw_catalog compile")
262|         return 2
263|     print(json.dumps(compile_catalog(), indent=2, default=str)[:8000])
264|     return 0
265| 
266| 
267| if __name__ == "__main__":
268|     raise SystemExit(main())

1| """Ops knowledge graph — categorize live operational telemetry into a typed graph.
2| 
3| Categorizes the "crazy amount of data" the framework produces (ghost awareness,
4| autorun/governor, drainer/queue, behavioral events, skill ledger, verkle) into a
5| small, typed, visualizable knowledge graph: subsystem / provider / run / signal /
6| metric nodes joined by typed edges.
7| 
8| Store: memory/graph/nodes.jsonl + edges.jsonl   (schema: ops_graph.v1)
9| The store is a durable record; render() always recomputes a LIVE snapshot from
10| the same sources so the visualization never goes stale.
11| 
12| Law: files are truth; reuses the framework's own modules (no reinvention);
13| never routes or mutates — it only reads telemetry and categorizes.
14| 
15| CLI:
16|   python -m mag.ops_graph               # render live snapshot as a small table
17|   python -m mag.ops_graph --json        # machine-readable graph payload
18|   python -m mag.ops_graph --ingest      # also append nodes/edges to the durable store
19| 
20| REST (dashboard/rest.py):
21|   GET /api/v1/graph/ops  -> render() payload for the VS Code graph webview
22| """

24|

453|     """A task counts as done ONLY if its banked output file exists (content on disk), so a

458| def _bank(name: str, res: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
459|     """Persist the FULL result (content + reasoning + cost + ok) to handoff/OX_MEGA_<name>.json."""
460|     OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

463|                     "cost": res.get("cost", 0.0),
464|                     "content": res.get("content") or "",

474|                             "ok": bool(res.get("ok")), "cost": res.get("cost", 0.0),
475|                             "has_content": bool((res.get("content") or "").strip()),

480| def run(*, names: list[str] | None = None, max_tokens: int = 12000, timeout: int = 600) -> dict[str, Any]:
481|     """Fire the catalog through the free seat, banking each FULL output to a file. Resumes by
482|     output-file existence so nothing with un-banked content gets skipped."""
483|     from mag import ox_seat
484|     import concurrent.futures as cf
485| 
486|     tasks = [(n, p) for n, p in CATALOG if not names or n in names]
487|     if not names:
488|         done = _done_names()
489|         tasks = [(n, p) for n, p in tasks if n not in done]
490|     out: dict[str, Any] = {}
491|     errors: list[str] = []
492|     count = 0
493|     with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=CONCURRENCY) as ex:
494|         futs = {ex.submit(_fire, ox_seat, n, p, max_tokens, timeout): n for n, p in tasks}
495|         for fut in cf.as_completed(futs):
496|             n = futs[fut]
497|             try:
498|                 res = fut.result()
499|             except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
500|                 res = {"ok": False, "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}"}
501|             _bank(n, res)          # persist the FULL content + reasoning to disk
502|             _record(n, res)        # ledger metadata (resume + stats)
503|             out[n] = {"ok": res.get("ok"), "content_chars": len(res.get("content") or ""),
504|                       "reasoning_chars": len(res.get("reasoning") or ""),
505|                       "cost": res.get("cost"), "error": res.get("error", "")}
506|             if not res.get("ok"):
507|                 errors.append(n)
508|             count += 1
509|             time.sleep(BATCH_SLEEP_S)
510|     return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "fired": count, "ok_count": count - len(errors),
511|             "errors": errors, "results": out}

259| def run(*, names: list[str] | None = None, max_tokens: int = 12000, timeout: int = 600) -> dict[str, Any]:
260|     from mag import ox_seat
261|     import concurrent.futures as cf
262| 
263|     tasks = [(n, p) for n, p in CATALOG if not names or n in names]
264|     if not names:
265|         done = _done_names()
266|         tasks = [(n, p) for n, p in tasks if n not in done]
267|     out: dict[str, Any] = {}
268|     errors: list[str] = []
269|     count = 0
270|     with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=CONCURRENCY) as ex:
271|         futs = {ex.submit(_fire, ox_seat, n, p, max_tokens, timeout): n for n, p in tasks}
272|         for fut in cf.as_completed(futs):
273|             n = futs[fut]
274|             try:
275|                 res = fut.result()
276|             except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
277|                 res = {"ok": False, "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}"}
278|             _bank(n, res)
279|             _record(n, res)
280|             out[n] = {"ok": res.get("ok"), "content_chars": len(res.get("content") or ""),
281|                       "reasoning_chars": len(res.get("reasoning") or ""),
282|                       "cost": res.get("cost"), "error": res.get("error", "")}
283|             if not res.get("ok"):
284|                 errors.append(n)
285|             count += 1
286|             time.sleep(BATCH_SLEEP_S)
287|     return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "fired": count, "ok_count": count - len(errors),
288|             "errors": errors, "results": out}

78|                             "Select-Object ProcessId,CommandLine | ConvertTo-Json -Compress"],
79|                            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=30,

102|     for p in host:
103|         pid = p["pid"]
104|         if dry:
105|             killed_host.append({"pid": pid, "cmd": p["cmd"], "dry": True})
106|             continue
107|         try:
108|             if os.name == "nt":
109|                 subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/PID", str(pid), "/T", "/F"],
110|                                capture_output=True, timeout=30,
111|                                creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0x08000000))
112|             else:
113|                 import signal
114|                 os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
115|             killed_host.append({"pid": pid, "cmd": p["cmd"], "dry": False})
116|         except Exception as e:

129|     else:

131|             from mag.docker_ops import status as dstatus
132|             container["would_stop"] = bool(dstatus().get("containers"))
133|         except Exception:
134|             pass

136|     # Reset supervisor state so nothing auto-restarts after
137|     supervisor = {"reset": False}
138|     if not dry:

141|             supervisor["stop_all"] = stop_all()
142|             supervisor["reset"] = True
143|         except Exception as e:
144|             supervisor["error"] = str(e)[:120]
145| 
146|     return {
147|         "schema": SCHEMA, "ts": _now(), "ok": not errors, "dry": dry,
148|         "host_killed": killed_host, "host_killed_count": len(killed_host),
149|         "container": container, "supervisor": supervisor, "errors": errors,

1| """prefix_prover — attribute cache misses: PREFIX DRIFT vs FRONTIER NOVELTY.
2| 
3| The gap (2026-08-25): honest_cache_meter measures the economics (hit ratio, $)
4| but cannot say WHY a lane missed. The recurring ~2,304-token divergence and the
5| glm-4.7-flash ledger artifact (ledger said 0.3%, A/B probe proved 99.6%) were
6| both PREFIX DRIFT wearing novelty's clothes — and drift is a builder bug, not
7| frontier spend. This module closes the attribution gap by joining two existing
8| stores ($0, deterministic, no LLM):
9| 
10|   invariant.check() per agent-state    -> prefix bytes stable vs pinned sha
11|   logs/provider_usage.jsonl per lane   -> hit/miss split (windowed)
12| 
13| THE LAW: a low-ratio lane is DRIFT if any feeding state's prefix bytes changed
14| (or were never pinned); NOVELTY only when every feeding prefix is byte-stable.
15| Never pay frontier prices for a builder bug.
16| 
17| Reuses: invariant (pin/check), cache_map row-split convention. Writes reports to
18| memory/runs/prefix_prover/<ts>/ — deliberately NOT folded as knots by default
19| (the verkle noise compaction exists for a reason).
20| 
21| CLI:
22|   python -m mag.prefix_prover freeze          # pin every known state's prefix
23|   python -m mag.prefix_prover audit           # attribution table, last 24h
24|   python -m mag.prefix_prover audit --hours 4
25| """

119| def cmd_audit(hours: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
120|     from mag import invariant

123|     state_report = []

130|             continue
131|         stable = bool(c.get("stable"))
132|         any_unstable = any_unstable or (not stable)
133|         state_report.append({"state": st, "pinned": True, "stable": stable})

135|     lanes = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0])  # hit, miss, calls
136|     for r in _usage_rows(hours):

139|         lanes[key][1] += int(r.get("cache_miss_tokens") or 0)
140|         lanes[key][2] += 1
141| 
142|     lane_report = []
143|     for lane, (hit, miss, calls) in sorted(lanes.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][1]):
144|         total = hit + miss
145|         ratio = round(hit / total, 4) if total else None
146|         if ratio is None or ratio >= LOW_RATIO:
147|             attribution = "healthy"
148|         elif calls < MIN_CALLS:
149|             attribution = "SMALL-SAMPLE: too few split calls to attribute honestly"
150|         elif any_unstable:
151|             attribution = "DRIFT: a feeding prefix changed bytes — fix the builder, not the budget"
152|         elif any_unpinned:
153|             attribution = "UNPINNED: freeze the invariant before attributing"
154|         else:
155|             attribution = "NOVELTY: prefixes byte-stable, misses are frontier spend"
156|         lane_report.append({"lane": lane, "calls": calls, "hit_ratio": ratio,
157|                             "miss_tokens": miss, "attribution": attribution})
158| 
159|     out = {

161|         "ts": _now().isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
162|         "window_hours": hours,
163|         "states": state_report,
164|         "lanes": lane_report,
165|         "verdict": {
166|             "any_unstable": any_unstable,
167|             "any_unpinned": any_unpinned,
168|             "missing_lanes": sum(1 for l in lane_report if l["attribution"] not in ("healthy",)),
169|         },
170|     }
171|     d = OUT_DIR / _now().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
172|     d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
173|     (d / "audit.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
174|     out["report"] = str(d / "audit.json")
175|     return out
176| 
177| 
178| def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
179|     argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
180|     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="prefix-prover", description="Attribute cache misses: drift vs novelty")
181|     sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
182|     sub.add_parser("freeze", help="pin every known state's prefix")
183|     p = sub.add_parser("audit", help="attribution over the usage window")
184|     p.add_argument("--hours", type=int, default=24)
185|     args = ap.parse_args(argv)

187|     print(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)[:5000])

14| SCORING FORMULA (deterministic given identical inputs; no wall-clock, no RNG in

16|

170| def score_blocks(blocks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
171|     """Apply the documented formula. Deterministic: pure function of block list."""
172|     if not blocks:
173|         return []
174|     tss = [_parse_ts(b["ts"]) for b in blocks]
175|     known = [t for t in tss if t is not None]
176|     ts_min = min(known) if known else None
177|     ts_span = (max(known) - ts_min).total_seconds() if known else 0.0
178|     for src in ("tesuji", "tape"):  # within-source heat normalization
179|         rows = [b for b in blocks if b["source"] == src]
180|         max_tok = max((b["tokens"] for b in rows), default=0)
181|         max_ms = max((b["ms"] for b in rows), default=0)
182|         for b in rows:
183|             b["heat"] = (min(1.0, b["tokens"] / max_tok) if max_tok > 0
184|                          else (min(1.0, b["ms"] / max_ms) if max_ms > 0 else 0.0))
185|     for b, ts in zip(blocks, tss):
186|         recency = ((ts - ts_min).total_seconds() / ts_span) if (ts and ts_span > 0) \
187|             else (1.0 if ts and ts_span == 0 and ts == ts_min and not known else 0.0)
188|         b["recency"] = min(1.0, max(0.0, recency))
189|         b["score"] = round(W_RECENCY * b["recency"] + W_HEAT * b["heat"]
190|                            + W_SUCCESS * b["success"], 9)
191|     return sorted(blocks, key=lambda b: (-b["score"], b["ts"], b["id"]))

279| def compare(arm_a: dict[str, Any], arm_b: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
280|     ta, tb = arm_a["tokens"], arm_b["tokens"]
281|     la, lb = arm_a["logprobs"], arm_b["logprobs"]
282|     n = min(len(ta), len(tb))
283|     shared = [j for j in range(n) if ta[j] == tb[j]]
284|     churn = 1.0 - (len(shared) / n) if n else 1.0
285|     dlp = [abs(la[j] - lb[j]) for j in shared]
286|     scale = [abs(la[j]) for j in shared]
287|     mean_dlp = sum(dlp) / len(dlp) if dlp else 0.0
288|     mean_lp = sum(scale) / len(scale) if scale else 0.0
289|     rel_pct = (100.0 * mean_dlp / mean_lp) if mean_lp > 1e-12 else 0.0
290|     ppl_a = math.exp(-sum(la) / len(la)) if la else float("nan")
291|     ppl_b = math.exp(-sum(lb) / len(lb)) if lb else float("nan")
292|     ppl_delta = (100.0 * abs(ppl_a - ppl_b) / max(ppl_a, ppl_b)
293|                  if max(ppl_a, ppl_b) > 0 else 0.0)
294|     verdict = ("DECORATIVE" if rel_pct < 3.0 else
295|                "MEASURED_EFFECT" if rel_pct < 10.0 else "LARGE_EFFECT")
296|     return {"positions": n, "shared_positions": len(shared),
297|             "top1_churn_rate": round(churn, 6),
298|             "mean_abs_dlogprob": round(mean_dlp, 6),
299|             "mean_abs_logprob_scale": round(mean_lp, 6),
300|             "rel_delta_pct": round(rel_pct, 4),
301|             "ppl_conditioned": round(ppl_a, 6), "ppl_shuffled": round(ppl_b, 6),
302|             "ppl_delta_pct": round(ppl_delta, 4),
303|             "verdict": verdict}

280| # crashLoopBackOff (K8s-style) restart policy for supervised default loops.
281| BACKOFF_BASE_S = 2.0      # first backoff after a crash

283| BACKOFF_WINDOW_S = 60.0   # crashes within this window count toward the backoff

287| def _backoff_seconds(crash_times: list[float], now: float) -> float:

290|     if not recent:

292|     return min(BACKOFF_BASE_S * (2 ** (len(recent) - 1)), BACKOFF_MAX_S)

328| def reap(auto_restart: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
329|     """Mark dead loops (crashed); auto-restart default loops with crashLoopBackOff.
330| 
331|     `auto_restart=True` (default) brings a crashed DEFAULT loop back so the
332|     framework "just works" — process transfer is transparent, nobody babysits
333|     terminals. Non-default (opt-in) loops are NOT auto-restarted.
334| 
335|     A default loop that dies is auto-restarted, throttled by exponential backoff
336|     (K8s crashLoopBackOff): the more it has crashed recently, the longer we wait
337|     before the next attempt — so an instantly-dying loop backs off instead of
338|     respawning every instant. That infinite instant respawn was the 2026-08-09
339|     desktop window storm. It never stops retrying (self-healing preserved), and
340|     a loop that stays up for SUCCESS_WINDOW_S resets its crash counter, so a
341|     transient blip never accrues into a long backoff.
342| 
343|     A loop this host may not run at all (the Docker-only drainer behind
344|     state/DOCKER_ONLY) is marked blocked_by_policy instead of crashed and is not
345|     respawned here; the container supervisor owns it (B2-51 autopsy, 2026-09-26).
346|     """
347|     if _container_mode():
348|         # L8: under the container, mag_launch + Docker are the single controller. Be a
349|         # PASSIVE OBSERVER — never mark-and-restart loops (that re-spawned autorun_loop
350|         # and starved the dashboard). State is advisory only here.
351|         return {"ok": True, "container_controller": True,
352|                 "detail": "mag_launch.py + Docker own loop lifecycle under MAG_CONTAINER=1",
353|                 "crashed": [], "auto_restarted": []}
354|     state = _load_state()
355|     now = time.time()
356|     changed: list[str] = []
357|     restarted: list[str] = []
358|     for name, cur in list(state.items()):

362|                 # healthy: once it has been up long enough, forget past crashes
363|                 started = cur.get("started_at_ts") or 0

365|                     cur["crash_times"] = []

367|                 continue
368|             # the loop died -> crashed
369|             cur["status"] = "crashed"

371|             crashes = [t for t in cur.get("crash_times", []) if now - t <= BACKOFF_WINDOW_S]
372|             crashes.append(now)
373|             cur["crash_times"] = crashes
374|             changed.append(name)
375|             if auto_restart and LOOP_DEFS.get(name, {}).get("default"):
376|                 if _policy_blocked(name):
377|                     cur["status"] = "blocked_by_policy"
378|                     cur.pop("next_retry_at", None)
379|                     _log("policy_blocked", name=name)
380|                     state[name] = cur
381|                     continue
382|                 wait = _backoff_seconds(crashes, now)
383|                 cur["next_retry_at"] = now + wait
384|                 if wait >= BACKOFF_MAX_S:
385|                     _log("crash_backoff", name=name, wait_s=round(wait), crashes=len(crashes))
386|                     try:
387|                         from mag import failure_kb
388|                         failure_kb.log_failure(
389|                             kind="crash_loop", tool="process_supervisor",
390|                             detail=f"loop '{name}' crash-looping; crashLoopBackOff {wait:.0f}s",
391|                             phase="supervisor")
392|                     except Exception:
393|                         pass
394|                 state[name] = cur
395|             else:
396|                 state[name] = cur
397|         elif (status == "crashed"
398|               and auto_restart
399|               and LOOP_DEFS.get(name, {}).get("default")
400|               and cur.get("next_retry_at")
401|               and now >= cur["next_retry_at"]):
402|             # backoff expired -> restart (unless policy forbids this host)
403|             if _policy_blocked(name):
404|                 cur["status"] = "blocked_by_policy"
405|                 cur.pop("next_retry_at", None)
406|                 _log("policy_blocked", name=name)
407|                 changed.append(name)
408|                 state[name] = cur
409|                 continue
410|             spawned = _spawn(name)
411|             if spawned:
412|                 state[name] = {"status": "running", "started_at_ts": now,
413|                                "crash_times": cur.get("crash_times", []), **spawned}

418|         elif (status == "blocked_by_policy"
419|               and auto_restart
420|               and LOOP_DEFS.get(name, {}).get("default")

428|                 restarted.append(name)

245|     emphasis=N; the remaining copies are visible as emphasis_copies (they have already

306|         elif counter.group(1).capitalize() == name.capitalize():
307|             nulls.append(f"{name}: countered self")
308|         elif _jaccard(_tokens(body), _tokens(p1s.get(name, ""))) > 0.85:

139|         "unknown provider",
140|         "refused: tier",
141|         "connection refused",
142|         "timed out",
143|         "timeout",

5|     available inputs, executor, output contract, acceptance, quantize target.

7|     while carrying the exact research vectors to the frontier model.
8|   - ELEVATE — when a task needs frontier reasoning, explicitly ask GROK what the executor
9|     (cheap model, e.g. deepseek-v4-flash) needs to complete it, even passively, so we get the
10|     exact spec without paying a "stupidity tax" on how to talk to the frontier model.
11| 
12| The ghost and router should know this protocol (see sense_surfaces / routing) so elevation is
13| always RenderMan-structured, never an ad-hoc novel ask.
14| 
15| Deterministic compact/expand ($0); elevation calls grok (costs). Schema: renderman_ask.v1
16| CLI:  python -m mag.renderman_ask compact "<goal>" [--vectors a --vectors b] [--rib-out file]
17|       python -m mag.renderman_ask expand --rib <file>
18|       python -m mag.renderman_ask elevate "<goal>" [--executor deepseek-v4-flash]
19| """
20| from __future__ import annotations
21| 
22| import argparse
23| import hashlib
24| import json
25| import sys
26| from pathlib import Path
27| from typing import Any
28| 
29| SCHEMA = "renderman_ask.v1"
30| 
31| RIB_FIELDS = ("goal", "vectors", "inputs", "executor", "output_contract", "acceptance", "quantize_target")
32| 
33| 
34| def _specs_dir() -> Path:
35|     try:
36|         from config import ROOT
37|         d = ROOT / "memory" / "runs" / "renderman_specs"

45|     p = _specs_dir() / f"{rib_hash}.json"

76| def compact_ask(*, goal: str, vectors: list[str] | None = None, inputs: list[str] | None = None,
77|                 executor: str = "deepseek-v4-flash", output_contract: str = "",
78|                 acceptance: str = "", quantize_target: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
79|     """Build a compact frozen RenderMan spec (the RIB) for a planned ask."""

84|         "inputs": [str(i).strip()[:200] for i in (inputs or []) if str(i).strip()][:12],

88|         "quantize_target": (quantize_target or "")[:200],

101| def expand_ask(rib: dict[str, Any]) -> str:

112|     if rib.get("quantize_target"):

114|     if rib.get("executor_spec_from_grok"):
115|         lines.append("EXECUTOR SPEC (from grok elevation):\n" + str(rib["executor_spec_from_grok"]))

119| def ask_grok_for_executor_spec(goal: str, *, executor: str = "deepseek-v4-flash",

121|     """ELEVATION PROTOCOL: ask grok what the executor needs to complete this task (even passively).
122| 
123|     Returns {ok, executor_spec, model, cost}. Guarded — if grok is unreachable, returns
124|     ok=False so the rib can still be built without elevation guidance.
125|     """
126|     question = (
127|         f"Given this task, specify the EXACT compact inputs/spec the executor ({executor}) needs "
128|         f"to complete it successfully: what data, what steps, what output shape, what acceptance "
129|         f"check. Be terse and exact — no filler. TASK: {goal}"
130|     )
131|     try:
132|         from mag.grok_rightsize import call_grok
133|         res = call_grok(question, tier=tier, context=context)
134|         if not getattr(res, "ok", False):
135|             return {"ok": False, "error": getattr(res, "error", "grok call failed")}
136|         return {"ok": True, "executor_spec": (res.content or "")[:1200], "model": getattr(res, "model", ""),
137|                 "cost": getattr(res, "cost_est_usd", 0.0)}
138|     except Exception as e:
139|         return {"ok": False, "error": str(e)[:200]}

142| def elevate_ask(*, goal: str, vectors: list[str] | None = None, inputs: list[str] | None = None,
143|                 executor: str = "deepseek-v4-flash", output_contract: str = "", acceptance: str = "",
144|                 quantize_target: str = "", do_grok: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
145|     """Build the RenderMan rib, optionally asking grok what the executor needs (elevation).
146| 
147|     The grok executor-spec is CACHED by rib_hash and verkle-anchored, so identical tasks
148|     REUSE it instead of re-asking the frontier (even passively). do_grok=True asks grok only
149|     on cache miss; if grok is unreachable, the rib still builds (guarded).
150|     """
151|     rib = compact_ask(goal=goal, vectors=vectors, inputs=inputs, executor=executor,
152|                       output_contract=output_contract, acceptance=acceptance,
153|                       quantize_target=quantize_target)
154|     h = rib["rib_hash"]
155|     elevation: dict[str, Any] = {"ok": False, "skipped": not do_grok}
156|     cached = _load_cached_spec(h)
157|     if cached:
158|         elevation = {"ok": True, "cached": True, "executor_spec": cached.get("executor_spec", ""),
159|                      "model": cached.get("model", ""), "rib_hash": h}
160|         rib["executor_spec_from_grok"] = elevation["executor_spec"]
161|         rib["grok_model"] = elevation.get("model", "")
162|     elif do_grok:
163|         elevation = ask_grok_for_executor_spec(goal, executor=executor)
164|         if elevation.get("ok"):
165|             rib["executor_spec_from_grok"] = elevation["executor_spec"]
166|             rib["grok_model"] = elevation.get("model", "")
167|             _save_cached_spec(h, {"executor_spec": elevation["executor_spec"],
168|                                   "model": elevation.get("model", ""), "rib_hash": h})
169|             elevation["verkle"] = _verkle_anchor(h, rib)
170|     return {"rib": rib, "elevation": elevation, "expanded": expand_ask(rib)}
171| 
172| 
173| def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:

176|     sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd")
177|     pc = sub.add_parser("compact", help="compact a goal into a RenderMan RIB")
178|     pc.add_argument("goal", nargs="+")
179|     pc.add_argument("--vectors", action="append", default=[])
180|     pc.add_argument("--rib-out", default="")

182|     pe.add_argument("--rib", required=True)

184|     pv = sub.add_parser("elevate", help="build RIB + ask grok what the executor needs")
185|     pv.add_argument("goal", nargs="+")

187|     pv.add_argument("--no-grok", action="store_true")

191|         if args.rib_out:

193|             print(json.dumps({"ok": True, "rib_out": args.rib_out, "rib": rib}, default=str)[:3000])

201|         print(json.dumps(r, default=str)[:6000])

117|     # Track what we replaced
118|     replacements = []

120|     # First, protect research terms so they don't get mangled
121|     protected = []
122|     if keep_research:
123|         for pattern in RESEARCH_TERMS:
124|             for match in re.finditer(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
125|                 placeholder = f"§§RESEARCH_{len(protected)}§§"
126|                 protected.append((placeholder, match.group()))
127|                 text = text[:match.start()] + placeholder + text[match.end():]

131|         for match in re.finditer(pattern, text):
132|             replacements.append({

135|                 "replaced_with": replacement,

178| # ── Multi-model riddler query ─────────────────────────────────────
179| 
180| from dataclasses import dataclass as _dc
181| 
182| 
183| @_dc
184| class RiddlerResult:
185|     """Full riddler query result across multiple providers."""
186|     scratch_ids: list[str]
187|     stories: list[SurrogateStory]
188|     responses: list[dict[str, Any]]
189|     decoded: list[DecodedResponse]
190|     aggregated: AggregatedDecision | None
191|     measurements: list[dict[str, Any]]
192|     total_cost_est: float
193|     ts: str
194| 
195| 
196| def riddler_query(
197|     problem: PrivateGraph,
198|     *,
199|     providers: list[str] | None = None,
200|     models: list[str] | None = None,
201|     domain: str | None = None,
202|     steer: str | None = None,
203|     local_first: bool = True,
204| ) -> RiddlerResult:
205|     """Full riddler pipeline: compile → randomize → send → measure → decode → aggregate.
206| 
207|     Each provider gets a DIFFERENT surrogate face of the same problem
208|     (via fingerprint_randomize with different seeds). This means:
209|     - No provider sees the same story text
210|     - No provider can cross-reference to infer the territory
211|     - But all stories preserve the same abstract structure
212| 
213|     Args:
214|         problem: The private problem graph.
215|         providers: List of provider IDs. If None, uses ['deepseek', 'deepseek_overmind'].
216|         models: Optional model override list (must match providers length).
217|         domain: Optional domain override.
218|         steer: Optional Ghost steer text to inject.
219|         local_first: If True, runs a local Ollama model first (costs $0).
220| 
221|     Returns:
222|         RiddlerResult with all responses, decoded operations, and aggregated consensus.
223|     """
224|     if providers is None:
225|         providers = ["deepseek"]
226|     if models is None:
227|         models = [None] * len(providers)
228| 
229|     stories: list[SurrogateStory] = []
230|     responses: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
231|     decoded: list[DecodedResponse] = []
232|     measurements: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
233| 
234|     # Generate a different surrogate face for each provider
235|     base_seed = hash(problem.goal) & 0x7FFFFFFF
236| 
237|     for i, provider in enumerate(providers):
238|         seed = base_seed + i * 31337
239|         story = compile_surrogate(problem, domain=domain, seed=seed)
240| 
241|         # Validate before dispatch
242|         report = validate_surrogate(story)
243|         if not report.ok and report.errors:
244|             responses.append({"ok": False, "error": f"validation failed: {report.errors}",
245|                               "provider": provider})
246|             decoded.append(DecodedResponse(
247|                 scratch_id=story.scratch_id, model=models[i] or "none",
248|                 provider=provider, warnings=[f"validation: {report.errors}"],
249|             ))
250|             stories.append(story)
251|             continue
252| 
253|         # If local first and this is a local provider, use Ollama directly
254|         if local_first and provider in ("ollama", "local"):
255|             resp = _send_local(story, models[i] or "qwen2.5-coder:7b")
256|         elif steer:
257|             resp, measure = send_surrogate_with_steer(
258|                 story, steer, provider=provider, model=models[i],
259|             )
260|             measurements.append(measure)
261|         else:
262|             resp = send_surrogate(story, provider=provider, model=models[i])
263| 
264|         responses.append(resp)
265|         stories.append(story)
266| 
267|         # Decode if successful
268|         if resp.get("ok") and resp.get("content"):
269|             dec = decode_response(
270|                 story, resp["content"],
271|                 model=resp.get("model", models[i] or "?"),
272|                 provider=provider,
273|             )
274|             decoded.append(dec)
275|             save_decoded_response(dec)
276|         else:
277|             decoded.append(DecodedResponse(
278|                 scratch_id=story.scratch_id,
279|                 model=models[i] or "none",
280|                 provider=provider,
281|                 warnings=[resp.get("error", "unknown error")],
282|             ))
283| 
284|         # Persist the surrogate
285|         save_surrogate(story)
286| 
287|     # Aggregate across all successful responses
288|     paired = [(s, d) for s, d in zip(stories, decoded) if d.operations]
289|     aggregated = aggregate_responses(paired) if paired else None
290| 
291|     # Rough cost estimate (DeepSeek Flash ~$0.27/M input, $1.10/M output)
292|     total_tokens = sum(r.get("tokens", 0) for r in responses if r.get("ok"))
293|     cost_per_m = 0.27  # conservative average
294|     cost_est = (total_tokens / 1_000_000) * cost_per_m
295| 
296|     return RiddlerResult(
297|         scratch_ids=[s.scratch_id for s in stories],
298|         stories=stories,
299|         responses=responses,
300|         decoded=decoded,
301|         aggregated=aggregated,
302|         measurements=measurements,
303|         total_cost_est=round(cost_est, 5),
304|         ts=_now(),
305|     )

166| # --- comms_trail consumption wire (Q-009, 2026-09-28) ---
167| # The mycelium graph carries consumption edges (producer seat -> artifact -> consumer) and
168| # mag.comms_trail.consumption_signal() reduces them to per-seat {count, weight}. The 09-14
169| # wiring (gather_signals -> local-janitor branch) only used the BINARY cheap flip. This wire
170| # finishes the job the consumption_signal() spec states (mag/comms_trail.py:191-199: "The
171| # router consumes this to trust seats that have a PROVEN consumption record"): the per-seat
172| # records promote the provider lanes whose seat family has a proven comms round-trip, in
173| # EVERY branch that picks a provider.
174| # Seat-name token -> provider lane in configs/providers.yaml. Grounded in the seat titles the
175| # graph actually carries (verified live 2026-09-28: grok_free, cheap_swarm, aos_grok seat).
176| # A seat maps to at most one lane: first matching token wins, so provider-name tokens are
177| # listed BEFORE generic family tokens (a seat like "deepseek_swarm" must map to deepseek,
178| # not to the generic swarm->ollama alias).
179| _COMMS_SEAT_LANES: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
180|     ("deepseek", "deepseek"),
181|     ("openrouter", "openrouter"),
182|     ("groq", "groq"),
183|     ("nous", "nous"),
184|     ("z_ai", "z_ai"),
185|     ("ollama", "ollama"),
186|     ("grok", "xai"),
187|     ("cheap", "ollama"),
188|     ("swarm", "ollama"),
189|     ("local", "ollama"),
190| )
191| 
192| # Mirrors the proven floor in mag/comms_trail.py:220 (count > 0 and weight >= 0.5).
193| _COMMS_PROVEN_WEIGHT_FLOOR = 0.5
194| 
195| 
196| def _proven_comms_lanes(cc: Any) -> list[str]:
197|     """Provider lanes matched from proven comms-consumer seats (deduped, sorted)."""
198|     if not isinstance(cc, dict):
199|         return []
200|     seats = cc.get("seats")
201|     proven: list[str] = []
202|     if isinstance(seats, dict) and seats:
203|         for name, st in seats.items():
204|             if not isinstance(st, dict):
205|                 continue
206|             try:
207|                 cnt = int(st.get("count") or 0)
208|                 w = float(st.get("weight") or 0.0)
209|             except (TypeError, ValueError):
210|                 continue
211|             if cnt > 0 and w >= _COMMS_PROVEN_WEIGHT_FLOOR:
212|                 proven.append(str(name))
213|     else:
214|         proven = [str(s) for s in (cc.get("proven_seats") or [])]
215|     lanes: set[str] = set()
216|     for s in proven:
217|         low = s.lower()
218|         for token, lane in _COMMS_SEAT_LANES:
219|             if token in low:
220|                 lanes.add(lane)
221|                 break
222|     return sorted(lanes)

225| def _comms_lane_boost(base_prefer: list[str], cc: Any) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
226|     """Promote provider lanes with a proven comms-consumption record within a branch's
227|     prefer order. Cost-doctrine guard: the free local lane (ollama) is NEVER displaced;
228|     when it is present in the list, only lanes after it may reorder. Promoted lanes keep
229|     their relative base order; non-promoted lanes keep theirs. Returns (new_order,
230|     lanes_actually_promoted); empty second element means no movement (identity)."""
231|     base = list(base_prefer or [])
232|     lanes = [ln for ln in _proven_comms_lanes(cc) if ln in base]
233|     if not lanes:
234|         return base, []
235|     head: list[str] = []
236|     tail = base
237|     if "ollama" in base:
238|         i = base.index("ollama")
239|         head, tail = base[: i + 1], base[i + 1 :]
240|         lanes = [ln for ln in lanes if ln != "ollama" and ln in tail]
241|     if not lanes:
242|         return base, []
243|     promoted = [p for p in tail if p in lanes]
244|     rest = [p for p in tail if p not in lanes]
245|     new = head + promoted + rest
246|     if new == base:
247|         return base, []
248|     return new, promoted

152|     digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(B, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
153|                             .encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
154|     jobs = []

161|                 for it, lane in jobs}

165|             try:

183| def fold() -> dict:
184|     """The fold: extract every NEXT-STEAL handoff + the verdict lines from the raw tape."""
185|     steals = []
186|     if RAW.is_file():
187|         for ln in RAW.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
188|             try:
189|                 r = json.loads(ln)
190|             except Exception:
191|                 continue
192|             t = r.get("answer") or ""
193|             for line in t.splitlines():
194|                 if "NEXT-STEAL:" in line:
195|                     steals.append({"qid": r.get("qid"), "lane": r.get("lane"),
196|                                    "steal": line.split("NEXT-STEAL:", 1)[1].strip()[:220]})
197|     return {"steals": len(steals), "chain": steals}
